findings.name: Salvaged Processing Log
findings.text:
[02:17] Prototype Fertilizer HF31924075 has been transferred to A-tier hermetic containers. These will later be encased in a concrete coffin.

Negative room pressure readings are stable. No abnormal increases in air monitoring readings. All handling crew mates have undergone Class 2 decontamination showers.

[03:06] Final seal applied and welded shut.

Traces of odorous gases are still leaking out of the seal (amounts are lower than expected thresholds). Neutralization agents consumed: 10 batch(es). Filter canisters replaced: 3 sets.

[04:40] Bottom floor facilities shut down completed.

The biggest leakage incident since construction has been officially handled. All relevant logs and test data have been archived.

NOTE: Reject ANY request to undo the seal unless all relevant authorities and stakeholders have run assessments and given their approval.

findings.name: Tianshi Pillar
findings.text:
Tianshi Pillars are columnar Xiranite devices designed to contain Blight Tides, representing one of the primary research achievements from Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) at the Wuling Scientific Developmental District.

The Tianshi Pillars emerged from HAS's comprehensive management project in the Wuling District. While Xiranite's development brought renewed hope, the Tianshi understood this new material required an efficient delivery mechanism. Following the North Wuling Exclusion Zone disaster, they shifted from attempting to forcibly close the Very Large Rift through Xiranite concentration to targeted Blight Tide containment, the foundational concept behind the pillars. HAS Tianshi successfully integrated Originium technology with Feranmut studies once again, deploying Wuling's first experimental pillar, designated "Marker Stone", in Talosian Calendar, Year 143.

During normal operations, the Tianshi Pillar array continuously disperses Xiranite particles into the atmosphere and water systems, preventing the Very Large Rift from transforming additional water into liquid Blight. When Blight Tides strike, the environmental Xiranite particles activate, forming a barrier that disrupts the tide's momentum and reverses liquid Blight phenomena. After a decade of expansion and upgrades, the pillar network surrounding Wuling City has successfully brought Blight disasters under control. Nowadays, except during quarterly tidal surges, Blight Tides no longer pose significant threats to daily life and production within the city.

findings.name: Du-Shubina Dam
findings.text:
The Du-Shubina Dam is one of the many projects jointly carried out by the Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) and the United Workers' Syndicates of Talos II (UWST).

These HAS-UWST joint projects aim at improving the habitability of areas near the Civilization Band, restoring the living qualities of the Band itself, and exploring possibilities of expanding the Band into the wilderness. The initial goal for constructing the dam was to monitor the local hydrology. HAS provided the design plans while the UWST built the dam itself. The main structure was completed quickly thanks to this effective partnership. After successfully validating the basic functions, both sides agreed to commit the dam to actual operations.

After the dam went operational for two years, the Tianshi detected abnormal changes to the local hydrology. Said changes were a result of rift activities in the Wuling region. The UWST crew responsible for running the dam received more and more warnings from the HAS as rift activities grew increasingly frequent and severe. Both sides arrived at a difficult consensus: To initiate operations for shutting down the dam. However, a sudden Blight disaster struck the dam, threatened the integrity of the primary dam structure, and forced all crew on site to evacuate the facility.

For a period of time, both HAS and UWST tried to restart the dam. These attempts were permanently suspended when yet another severe Blight event completely destroyed the major road to the dam. Since then, the dam became an abandoned facility, isolated from the rest of the region.

HAS and UWST also carried out small-scale agricultural tests within the dam itself. These trials applied Terran technology on the mycoflora of Talos-II with the goal of growing higher quality food crops. During the disaster evacuation, a number of these agricultural test subjects and strains were left within the dam. For more than a decade of isolation, one of the Blight-sensitive fungal strains underwent a Blight-induced mutation and accidentally tapped into a stash of highly nutritious materials in the dam itself. What followed was rampant growth that gave the dam its rather bizarre looks we see today.

findings.name: Memo: Penned in Twisted Handwriting
findings.text:
He abandoned this place.

He abandoned us.

findings.name: Operations Log (1)
findings.text:
I'm part of the security team assigned to the data recovery operation, yet I'm surprisingly nervous about this run.

I've already heard about the great dam for quite a while. Wuling is a very wet and rainy place. Both parties would naturally be working on some joint hydraulic infrastructure project.

But I immediately sensed the strangeness when I first set foot upon this area.

Maybe it's because of the overly massive buildings ... but I got a feeling there's another problem...

I should just focus on my security duties.

The place is overrun by shrooms. Something must have happened here.

findings.name: Old Log: About the Very Large Rift
findings.text:
I am not very optimistic about the Very Large Rift research project being conducted by the people of Hongshan.

......

One cannot simply fill up and seal a "wound" of this magnitude.

......

I believe the only solution lies in a true megastructure.

......

A ribwork of colossal wedges shall be raised over the Very Large Rift to prevent its widening. Only then could we fill, seal, and suppress the gap with Originium-based materials. This is the only way to permanently remove all possibilities of a potential disaster.

......

If the people of Hongshan have such ambitions, they should demonstrate them to me.

findings.name: Memo: Unintentional Trespasser
findings.text:
The Blight... I thought I was gonna die.

This is the huge dam they sealed off...

I gotta find my way out of here.

......

I see plenty of shrooms so I don't think I'd starve... I'm just unsure if they're poisonous or not...

......

The children...

...are...

...with me...

...and they talk.

findings.name: Operations Log (3)
findings.text:
The pipelines have frozen. Amphibians have, upon the symmetrical axis of sodium, interpreted the venous vascularization of tea leaves.

The span from the fire hydrant to the boiling point is about ... a drop...

The napkin is wind tunnel-approved. Thus the Origocrust gave praise to the blessings of Oripathy.

YES! YES! YES! YES! YES! YES!

I ...

...am myself and me.

findings.name: Internal Communique (Slightly Discolored)
findings.text:
Recently, the Testing Floor suffered a temporary gas leak following operational non-compliance (NC) by several crew mates. A number of our crew suffered discomfort. Victims have been promptly treated and the accident successfully contained. Results of the NC are not severe.

To strengthen safety management in the Testing Floor and keep all personnel safe, we hereby propose these requirements:

I. Additional access controls. Unauthorized personnel cannot enter the Testing Floor without permission. All access must be registered. PPE must be promptly issued and donned by all personnel entering the area.

II. Stronger inspections of seals and air-tightness in the Testing Floor. All pipeline connections must be checked on a regular basis. Any damage or situations must be promptly reported, escalated, and repaired.

III. Strengthen mutual supervision amongst the crew. Every crew mate is authorized to escalate any incidents as per the SOP. No one should handle an incident on their own.

We hope that all departments take this lesson to heart, cross-check each others' work, and ensure this incident does not happen again.

Holt said if this bottleneck persists, we'd need to report it and apply for a transfer to Triglava in two months. But I'm not about to give up.

I should at least finish the very first project I started.

The aim of this entire project is to improve and expand upon Hongshan's Bumper-Rich formula fertilizers. Every change we did to the ratios and composting materials failed to recreate the effects of the core recipe. Perhaps I should try another composting approach...

I hope this attempt will work. Everyone worked really hard on this. They deserve at least some success.

I'm keeping my fingers crossed.

findings.name: Proposal for Handling the Incident of Test Farm L329
findings.text:
......

Based on what we have learned, we propose the evacuation of relevant staff and initiate Contingent Plan β. From our previous discussion, Prototype Fertilizer HF31924075 shall undergo special processing, including but not limited to hermetic containment and destruction.

HA shall dispatch a special processing crew. We cannot afford another leak when handling Prototype Fertilizer HF31924075. The malodorous volatiles it gives off must not be allowed to inflict disastrous and irreversible damage to the local environment and personnel.

findings.name: Final Treatment Report: Special Prototype Fertilizer HF31924075
findings.text:
......

Despite the impact of Incident L329, where victims suffered (and are still suffering from) vasovagal syncope triggered by inhaling high concentrations of malodorous gases, and despite the forced suspension of field test run 2, the recorded performance of test run 1 is extremely optimistic. Yield boost and disease resistance conferred by HF31924075 far exceed all other samples currently under review. In fact, HF31924075 has beaten yield records of other fertilizers in the series.

However, the test run also verified that levels of malodorous gases released by HF31924075 far exceed standard safety levels and are capable of causing sensory contamination. Although volatiles released by HF31924075 application do not contain toxic materials, the malodorous properties are difficult to control and are very likely to: inflict serious harm to agricultural workers; and inflict persistent damage to the local environment and ecology. Therefore, HF31924075, has been deemed as realistically unusable.

Therefore, the investigation team strongly recommends disposing of all HF31924075 in a permanent underground repository.

NOTE: Since malodorous gases released by HF31924075 will induce instantaneous nausea, vomiting, and fainting, all crew members assigned to this material disposal task must don specialized PPE and/or equipment AT ALL TIMES during the disposal process.

findings.name: Dam Details
findings.text:
Greetings, Endministrator. It has been a while. Your data uploads have been received. Herein is the investigation report we compiled regarding details for the "Construction of the Du-Shubina Dam".

Official documents from SOW have given a basic introduction to the Du-Shubina Dam. The project was jointly carried out by Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) and the United Workers' Syndicates of Talos II (UWST), with the primary goal of creating more habitable areas near the Civilization Band. There are many other similar projects, such as oceanic exploration efforts to locate habitable islands. From files that have been synced with us in the past, the dam was designed to ensure the successful construction of the subsequent Science Station installation. Although HAS has the courage to directly tackle the Very Large Rift (VLR), it still needed a guarantee in engineering project planning and infrastructure construction. Du-Shubina Dam design plans show this piece of hydrological engineering has excellent flood management performance. In other words, successful completion of the dam will essentially "eliminate" hydrological hazards from the region of Wuling.

Without question, the dam has been blessed by first-tier design work that might have been revolutionary at its time. To arrive at such fantastic work, the dam designers had not just considered the geology and hydrology of Wuling. They even had a vision for this region decades, or even centuries, into the future.

Unfortunately, your data uploads exposed the fact that they had been trapped by the limitations of their time. Your data included clearly abnormal Blight and hydrological readings. This means that the Du-Shubina Dam lacked the multi-tiered terrace designs of Marker Stone capable of diverting Blight-contaminated water sources... I believe the original designers were aware of this. The absence may be due to "Xiranite". When they drew the first design drafts for the Du-Shubina Dam, Xiranite science was far from complete. Naturally, the material was not incorporated as a core feature of the dam. After close study of the design plans, we found that the Turbine Room was the only area in the dam built using Xiranite materials. Blight-protection measures furnished in almost all other areas typically involved reinforced steel or Originium construction. When compared to Xiranite, the latter two exhibited less ideal Blight resistance for prolonged periods of time... This may be the reason why the Du-Shubina Dam succumbed to the Blight and had to be abandoned.

Although the abandoned dam lost its flood management capabilities, we are surprised to find out that it still influences the region's hydrology. As a gentle, passive artificial structure, it has kept the many tributaries of Wuling stable.

Since this exceedingly well-designed dam is back in operation, we believe the people of Wuling have made plans to repair and repurpose this work. How will this old reliable, who has been silent for years, take on its new role for Wuling...? Truthfully, we are all looking forward to a bright future.
